prerequisites: Knowledge of Mechanics (Static equilibrium of a rigid body: Equilibrium conditions of a rigid body, Center of gravity, Couple of forces, Constraint forces).
Knowledge of Statics, Vector Calculus, Geometry of sections, Differentiation and Integration, Differential equations.

learning_outcomes.text: Characterize the different elements of manufacturing processes.
Understand the concepts of stress and strain, and relate them through constitutive equations.
Calculate and represent internal force diagrams in bars and structures.
Solve torsion problems in shafts and three-dimensional structures.
Solve combined bending problems in beams and structures.
Understand the phenomenon of buckling in bars and solve bar buckling problems.

syllabus_topics: Object and purpose of Strength of Materials.
Concept of elastic solid.
Theoretical solid model used in Strength of Materials. Mechanical prism.
Static equilibrium and elastic equilibrium.
State of stresses and strains in a mechanical prism.
General principles of Strength of Materials.
Relationships between stresses and strains.
Internal forces: their relationships with the components of the stress matrix.
Types of external loads on a mechanical prism.
Reactions of constraints. Types of supports.
Statically determinate and indeterminate systems.
Notion of safety factor. Allowable stress.
Theory of internal potential or elastic strain energy.
Energy theorems.
Strength criteria. Concept of equivalent stress.
Geometry of plane sections: center of gravity, moments of inertia, radius of gyration, principal moments of inertia. Calculation of principal moments of inertia using Mohr's circle.
Normal force and stress state of a mechanical prism subjected to uniaxial tension or compression.
State of deformations due to uniaxial tension or compression.
Stresses and strains produced in a straight prism subjected to variable axial load.
Stresses and strains produced in a straight prism by its own weight.
Expression of the internal potential of a mechanical prism subjected to uniaxial tension or compression.
Statically indeterminate uniaxial tension or compression.
Uniaxial tension or compression produced by thermal variations or assembly defects.
Biaxial tension or compression. Thin-walled shells of revolution.
Triaxial tension or compression.
Introduction to General Theory of Bending. Stress Analysis.
Pure bending. Navier's law.
Simple bending. Plotting internal force diagrams.
Relationships between shear force, bending moment, and load.
Stresses produced in simple bending by shear force. Colignon's theorem.
Principal stresses in simple bending. Graphical construction of Mohr's circle to determine principal stresses and principal directions in simple bending.
Study of shear stresses in the case of thin-walled sections subjected to simple bending.
Thin-walled sections with a vertical principal axis that is not an axis of symmetry.
Shear center.
Introduction to General Theory of Bending. Strain Analysis.
Double integration method for determining the deflection of straight beams subjected to simple bending. Equation of the elastic curve.
Universal equation of the deformed shape of a beam with constant stiffness.
Mohr's theorems.
Expression of the internal potential of a mechanical prism subjected to simple bending.
Concept of reduced section.
Deformations due to shear forces.
Dummy load method for calculating deformations.
Introduction to Skew Bending and Combined Bending.
Skew bending in the elastic domain. Stress analysis.
Expression of the internal potential of a mechanical prism subjected to skew bending. Strain analysis.
Combined bending.
Eccentric tension or compression. Center of pressure.
Central core of the section.
Introduction to Statically Indeterminate Bending.
Calculation of single-span indeterminate beams.
Continuous beams.
Statically indeterminate systems. Degree of indeterminacy of a system.
Force method for calculating statically indeterminate systems.
Application of Castigliano's theorem for solving statically indeterminate systems.
Construction of bending moment, shear force, and normal force diagrams in statically indeterminate systems.
Calculation of deformations and displacements in statically indeterminate systems.
Symmetry and antisymmetry in statically indeterminate systems.
Introduction to Theory of Torsion.
Elementary theory of torsion in prisms of circular cross-section.
Determination of torsional moments. Calculation of power transmission shafts.
Expression of the internal potential of a mechanical prism subjected to pure torsion.
Combined loading of simple bending and torsion.
Torsion in straight mechanical prisms of non-circular cross-section.
Experimental study of torsion by membrane analogy.
Torsion of thin-walled sections.
Combined bending and torsion.
Mohr's method for calculating displacements in the case of combined loads.
Introduction to Lateral Bending. Buckling.
Stability of elastic equilibrium. Notion of critical load.
Buckling of straight bars of constant cross-section subjected to compression. Euler's formula.
Critical load value according to bar support type. Buckling length.
Limits of applicability of Euler's formula.
Calculation of bars of constant cross-section subjected to centered compression according to the Technical Building Code.
Strength of Materials exercises.
Strength of Materials problem-solving sessions.
assessment_rules: A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required in the final written test for it to be averaged, and a minimum weighted average of 5 out of 10 across all assessment systems is needed to pass the course. If the minimum score of 4 in the written test is not met, the final grade will be 'Fail' and capped at 4.5 points. Unpassed parts can be re-evaluated in subsequent calls, except for 'Observation techniques' and 'Assignments and projects' which are continuous assessment components performed once per academic year.
